chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Murazim, from a man, from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who seeks the little sustenance, that would be inviting him to bringing a lot (a bigger amount) from the sustenance; (and the one who neglects a little (sale/project/income) from the sustenance, that would be inviting him to the going away of a lot from the sustenance)'.

key_terms.دَاعِيَهُ: Inviting him, serving as a cause or catalyst for him

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and practical significance of seeking small sustenance in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that actively seeking out small amounts of sustenance (rizq) serves as a catalyst to attract greater abundance, while neglecting or ignoring small opportunities leads to the loss of significant wealth. This hadith emphasizes the ethical and practical importance of diligence in livelihood and not overlooking minor sources of income. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is often interpreted through the lens of 'barakah' (divine blessing), where gratitude and effort in small matters unlock larger provisions, reflecting the principle that rizq is not merely material but spiritually contingent upon one's engagement with the world.

en.hubeali: Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Muhammad Bin Murazim, from a man, from Ishaq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who seeks the little sustenance, that would be inviting him to bringing a lot (a bigger amount) from the sustenance; (and the one who neglects a little (sale/project/income) from the sustenance, that would be inviting him to the going away of a lot from the sustenance)’.
en.sarwar: 29. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Ya’qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Murazim from a man from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘

If one searches for little amounts of sustenance it leads to attract greater amounts of sustenance, and if one gives up small amounts of sustenance it leads to going away of the greater amount of sustenance.’”
